title: Projectile rendering: shared materials and meshes, node pooling, pooled lights
player_outcome: Magic weapons, guns and bosses that fire many projectiles no longer hitch or drop frames; glowing shots still light their surroundings near the camera.
design: Checked in code: ProjectileRenderer.Create makes a new StandardMaterial3D, a new Sphere or CapsuleMesh and a new OmniLight3D per projectile, and QueueFrees it on removal (ProjectileRenderer.cs:91-148).
Cache Dictionary<(Color, float), StandardMaterial3D> glow materials, sphere meshes keyed by radius in mm, and a single bullet capsule mesh.
Pool nodes per def id: on Removed, hide and push (cap 32 per def, QueueFree beyond that); reset transforms on reuse. Minion and creature projectiles use the AssetCache CreatureVisual path.

Lights: new partial game/Entities/ProjectileRenderer.Lights.cs owns N OmniLight3D, with N from the new GraphicsPreset.ProjectileLights. Each frame they go to the lit projectiles nearest the camera; no per-projectile lights.
data_changes: data/config/graphics.json: projectileLights low 0, medium 4, high 8, ultra 12
tests: combat.cmds: wield a magic weapon and fire 40 times, then `assert projectiles.nodes_created <= 34`
verification: Rendering run: rapid-fire weapon plus a boss volley; F3 draw calls stable; `perf spikes` free of gd.projectiles
Visual: nearby bolts still cast light; distant ones glow only
risks: Pooled creature minions must reset animation and tint state
graphics.json and GraphicsConfig.cs are shared with P1b-11 and P1a
